title: OMP2MPI: Automatic MPI code generation from OpenMP programs
review_status: full-text audit complete; supported transformation patterns, correctness checks, PolyBench setup, 16/32/64-core scaling and unsupported constructs checked
sections_checked: Speedup against sequential and OpenMP versions
Conclusion/future support for shared variables and critical/atomic constructs
venue_year_verified: arXiv first submitted 2015-02-10; v2 dated 2015-06-11; venue identified as CoRR/arXiv, no peer-reviewed venue paper located in this audit
evidence_note: The tool focuses on OpenMP parallel loops. Selected PolyBench cases on 64 Bull CPU cores show >20x versus sequential in most cases and >4x versus original OpenMP; correctness is checked on microbenchmarks. Authors list additional shared-variable and critical/atomic constructs as future work.

title: Program Generation for Small-Scale Linear Algebra Applications
review_status: full-text audit complete; DSL scope, code-generation pipeline, baselines, numerical workloads, hardware/cache conditions, repetition protocol and fixed-size limitations checked
sections_checked: Single-threaded Sandy Bridge setup, warm cache, 30 repetitions
Results against libraries/compilers and application variation
evidence_note: Reports strong routine-level gains for fixed-size small linear algebra on a single-thread Intel Core i7-2600 with warm cache and working set in L1/L2; results vary across applications (GPR roughly matches MKL). Authors explicitly restrict to fixed sizes/full structured storage and single input; multicore, batching and general sizes are future work.

title: TreeGen: A Tree-Based Transformer Architecture for Code Generation
review_status: full-text audit complete; HearthStone/ATIS/GEO data, exact match/BLEU/manual Acc+, neural and non-neural baselines, ablations and absence of execution-based correctness testing checked
sections_checked: ATIS/GEO comparison with neural and CCG baselines
venue_year_verified: arXiv first submitted 2019-11-07; peer-reviewed AAAI 2020, 34(05), 8984–8991, DOI 10.1609/aaai.v34i05.6430; sample stratum uses arXiv first-submission year
evidence_note: Reports 4.5 percentage-point improvement on HearthStone over previous best with structural preprocessing; 89.1/89.6 on ATIS/GEO and best among neural systems, but slightly below non-neural WKZ14 on semantic parsing. Uses exact sequence, BLEU and manually assessed renaming-tolerant Acc+; no executed behavioral test results in the paper.

title: CodeBLEU: a Method for Automatic Evaluation of Code Synthesis
review_status: targeted full-text metric follow-up inspected via primary arXiv PDF; BLEU/exact-match limitations, AST/data-flow score, three-task human-correlation study and task-specific exception checked
sections_checked: Introduction: BLEU, exact match and computational accuracy limitations
Three task protocols and 10-judge/50-example-per-task human ratings
venue_year_verified: arXiv v2 dated 2020-09-27; targeted source is the primary full-text PDF
evidence_note: CodeBLEU correlates with human ratings at 0.977/0.970/0.979 across text-to-code, code translation and refinement, but exact accuracy correlates more strongly for code refinement (0.999). Human ratings cover 50 randomly selected examples per task and 10 judges. CodeBLEU is not executable equivalence.
